title: Bounded constant finite-module models for good lower truncations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a precoverage $J$ containing isomorphisms and stable under composition and base change, with the required pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $R$ be the underlying ring sheaf of the constant commutative-ring sheaf with value $B$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For a $B$-module $M$, write $c(M)$ for its constant module presheaf sheafified along the constant-ring sheafification unit [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $P$ be a cochain complex of $R$-module sheaves such that $H^j(P)=0$ above some integer and every $H^j(P)$ is locally constant of finite type [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-site-locally-constant-finite-type]. For every integer $a$ and object $V$ there is a covering sieve $S$ on $V$ such that for every arrow $f:U\to V$ in $S$ there is a complex $M^\bullet$ of $B$-modules, an integer $b$, and an isomorphism in the standard derived category of $R|_U$-modules
$$(\tau_{\ge a}P)|_U\simeq c(M^\bullet)|_U.$$
Every term $M^j$ is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $M^j=0$ for $j<a$ or $b<j$. Here truncation is good lower truncation [def-kun-truncations], realization is termwise including differentials, and restriction is to the slice site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No points of the site or finite projective dimension is assumed.

proof.text: Choose an upper cohomological bound b for P. Exact restriction commutes with cohomology and good truncation. The lower truncation therefore has cohomology only in [a,b], and its retained cohomology has the same local constant descriptions. If a>b, its cohomology is all zero, so the zero complex is a model.

Apply the proved arbitrary-site constant-ring module-sheaf equivalence. It retains the additive sheaf and naturally identifies constant-module realizations. It is exact because equivalences preserve kernels and cokernels.

The equivalence respects restriction and constant realization: each restricted scalar action is along the restriction of the same ring unit. For constants, the sheafification unit identifies the two constructions; uniqueness in the sheafification adjunction makes the identification natural in every B-linear map. Thus it also identifies the differentials and the termwise complex realizations. Relocalization identifies iterated slices with the slice at the composite arrow.

On the slice over V the identity arrow is terminal. Apply the bounded constant model theorem to the transported lower truncation, with cohomology interval [a,b]. Transport its bounded finite-module complex models back through the exact equivalence and the natural comparisons just constructed. This gives a covering family of V and the claimed models on its members.

Take the sieve generated by that family. An arrow in it factors through a member of the family. Further restrict its model using the natural constant-restriction comparison. The module complex, finite terms, and interval bound are unchanged. The generated sieve is covering; empty slices admit the zero model.

theorem exists_site_bounded_truncation_models
    (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition]
    [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks]
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (𝓡(J.toGrothendieck, B))) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (P.homology j))
    (hlc : ∀ j : ℤ, IsLocallyConstantFiniteType J.toGrothendieck B (P.homology j))
    (a : ℤ) (V : C) :
    ∃ S : Sieve V, S ∈ J.toGrothendieck V ∧
      ∀ (U : C) (f : U ⟶ V), S f →
        letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (SheafOfModules.{u} ((𝓡(J.toGrothendieck, B)).over U))
        ∃ (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ) (b : ℤ),
          (∀ j : ℤ, j < a ∨ b < j → IsZero (E.X j)) ∧
          (∀ j : ℤ, Module.Finite B (E.X j)) ∧
          Nonempty
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
                (((overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J.toGrothendieck, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex
                  (.up ℤ)).obj (P.truncGE a)) ≅
              DerivedCategory.Q.obj
                ((((cB(J.toGrothendieck, B)) ⋙
                  overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J.toGrothendieck, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex
                    (.up ℤ)).obj E))
